- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 77.5+ values), then corrects with a downward bias later.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or lagged response to recent price drops.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing the true “tail” of the price curve.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices (e.g., >78.0).
- Forecasts show less sensitivity to recent low prices (e.g., 75.0–76.0) compared to recent highs.
- Horizon-specific: 1–3 day forecasts are overconfident; 20+ day forecasts show more lag and underestimation.
- Model fails to capture “rebound” after sharp declines — often underestimates recovery phase.
- Forecasts are not calibrated to the true volatility — overestimates volatility in early days, underestimates in late days.
